title: Criteria and Process to Prefer Charges for Capital Offences
what_it_is: Criteria and Process to Prefer Charges for Capital Offences

sections.label: Holding charge for capital offence
sections.summary: A holding charge is tendered in Court when preliminary investigations reveal a capital offence may have been committed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In cases where preliminary investigations reveal that a capital offence may have been committed by an accused person, a holding charge will be tendered against the accused person in Court.

sections.label: AGC prosecutorial discretion review
sections.summary: AGC reviews evidence and circumstances holistically before deciding whether to proceed with a capital charge, lesser charges, or withdraw.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: AGC will review the evidence and the circumstances of the case holistically, before exercising its prosecutorial discretion to decide on an appropriate course of action – whether to proceed with the capital charge, lesser charge or charges, or to withdraw the charge.

sections.label: Amended charges and sentences
sections.summary: Charges were amended to rioting, rioting with a deadly weapon, and culpable homicide not amounting to murder, with sentences matching roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: After consideration of the evidence available and the roles played by the accused persons in the incident, the charges were amended to rioting for those who had known that there would be a fight, but did not know that others in their group were armed; rioting with a deadly weapon for those who had known that there would be a fight and that others in their group were armed; and culpable homicide not amounting to murder for those armed and actively attacking the victim.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In line with their respective roles in the incident, the accused persons in the first group received sentences of about three to five years’ imprisonment and three to six strokes of the cane; those in the second group received sentences of five to six years’ imprisonment and six strokes of the cane; and those in the third group received sentences of seven to 12 years’ imprisonment and five to 12 strokes of the cane.

sections.label: Sentences for abrasions and aggravating factors
sections.summary: Ang Da Yuan, Natalie Siow and Joel Tan faced fines only, but aggravating factors led to imprisonment sentences.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As only abrasions were caused, Ang Da Yuan, Natalie Siow and Joel Tan would have been liable for a fine only, based on the sentencing guidelines set in a High Court judgment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, taking into account the aggravating factors, such as their involvement in group violence and the public disquiet caused given that the fight took place in public, Natalie Siow and Joel Tan were given one months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As Ang Da Yuan had previously been convicted of violent crime offences, he was given a higher sentence of two months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Ang Da Yuan was given another six months' imprisonment and six strokes of the cane, while Natalie Siow was given another five months' imprisonment which was served concurrently with the other sentence, but no caning as she is a female.

sections.label: Conditional warning for consorting
sections.summary: Chan Jia Xing tried to stop the fight and was co-operative, receiving a 12-month conditional warning for consorting.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Chan Jia Xing tried to stop the fight and was co-operative with Police investigations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Hence, he was given a 12-month conditional warning for consorting with a person carrying an offensive weapon.

sections.label: Harbouring and hurt charges
sections.summary: A charge of voluntarily causing hurt with dangerous weapon was considered, and "B" was sentenced for harbouring offenders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Another charge of voluntarily causing hurt with dangerous weapon with common intention was taken into consideration for sentencing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Fourth, "B" was charged with harbouring of offenders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: He was sentenced to one year six months' imprisonment, and another charge of abetment of voluntarily causing hurt was taken into consideration for sentencing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Overall, the offenders' charges in this case reflected the premeditated plan to attack the deceased, their respective culpability and involvement and the sentences imposed were similarly consistent with sentencing benchmarks.
